Source: issue #880, owner decisions 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-09 (review by Fable and Fable 5.2). PR numbers are the PRs of the plan. State: 2026-11-09 late night, 43 PRs merged.

Why the interfaces are too lax today (FACT, origin/main)
Record.area and Record.kind are free strings; Record.data is
no schema generated from Rust: two hand-written type sets.
Python owns store, model and check: ir/ 34 145 lines
check/ 28 878 lines; check imports ir.model 78 times.
The host decodes the whole reply once (json.loads): 2.7 to
2.9 GiB on x35 with the Python and the native collector.
Rules today: native/layers.toml + a pytest (AD-327); cargo deny;
one binary per language in the platform wheel (AD-317).
Python shell: CLI, MCP, Studio, render and views; check only until its rule families move into the core (WP6)
ONE SEAM: every type defined once in Rust, schema generated, a published schema never changes. Form decided by WP2 (JSON read-set, PyO3 or evaluation in core).
Rust core · declared in native/architecture-contract.json and checked by ArchKeel itself (WP-C)
contract vocabulary as Rust types, Python types generated;
matching logic and invariants ported by hand first
rule families move one by one (read-set order);
each deletes its Python code; golden verdict maps
validate once: ids, coverage, paths, references,
PASS only from a bundled or pinned producer (WP4)
protocol 10 = serde types, kinds closed per version,
newtype ids, producer identity, reason codes,
files, paths, symlink, size and depth limits:
one rule set for every collector (PR 5 slice 0a)
Core v1 = collectors, facts, store and cache (WP3a, WP4). Core v2 = model and rule evaluation (WP6). External collectors (collector_argv) reach the store
like any producer, but give at most UNKNOWN. Python keeps no second copy of a type and does not validate core output again (version and digest only).
Plan after the architecture review: work packages and gates
Process: merge-tree and file-set script in tools/, Full before any output-changing merge, false-PASS probe suite in the repo (Full), no up-to-date rule
TypeScript: stack 3a to 3d (reviewed) -> 4.3a-4/5 on today's wire (typed internals) -> 4.4 switch (probes + owner + host peak not above Python) -> 4.5 delete
Contract for native/: declare the target crates (facts, store, model, eval) before their code; replaces layers.toml (needs 5b-2 module edges)
Concept inventory: closed enums, ids, field read-set per check module, proofs with a reader (also on TypeScript), all ir codecs, model logic
Seam measurement: full reply, read-set, without excerpts; JSON, facts and RawRecord peaks apart; decide JSON subset, PyO3 or evaluation in core
Protocol 10: serde types, generated published schema, kinds closed per version (+ versioned extension), producer identity, reason codes
One collector process per command, result cache
Rust store, scope from WP2: generic validation once, all ir codecs recounted, Python codecs deleted in the same PR
Python collector (PR 5) and Dart (PR 8) on protocol 10; Python source proofs die with the Python collector, one false-PASS probe per proof
Rule families into the core in read-set order; model logic ported by hand, then model types generated; golden verdict maps per family
1 PASS only from a bundled or pinned producer with recorded identity; an external collector gives at most UNKNOWN. 2 First native PASS and the benchmark before protocol 10.
3 The PyO3 threshold is decided from the WP2 numbers (20 % stays the default). 4 The end state includes rule evaluation in Rust; Python stays the CLI, MCP, Studio and report shell.
5 The 4.4 switch has the publish gate: probes, owner confirmation, host peak not above the Python collector. 6 facts_validation is split: generic checks move to the store, Python proofs die.
Stops: IR steps S4 to S6 in Python, host levers P2 and P5, any Python validation rework. The 19 bottom ir modules are frozen in behaviour (golden replies); bug fixes stay allowed.

Rust core: one type model (v1 store, v2 model and rules)
New goal (owner, 2026-11-09). WP0 to WP6 planned; Python IR steps S1 to S3 and two S4 splits are merged, S4 to S6 stop.
Done. 39 PRs merged. Rust rules in the gate (#904), no module cycles (#907).
CI time budget (owner): a target, not a gate
#919 meets it without queue: PR 7.3 to 8.2 min, Full 12.6 to 15.2 min. Queue: Free plan, 20 jobs.
Honest reading: 6 of 10 violations fixed. The bottleneck now is the merge queue: 7 PRs are done or nearly done and wait for CI runs.
Violations found on 2026-11-09 and what they mean for the goal and the plan
Numbers in the diagram: where each violation sits (red open, green fixed).
False PASS in 5b-1 (#916) over 5 review rounds: scopes, shadowing, macros, attributes
Not merged. Now sound by construction: a local name equal to a crate name, or any crate name in a macro, attribute or string without an edge, is UNKNOWN.
5b-1: memory n squared (19 GB from 640 KB), stack abort, symlink read outside root
Every binary needs the AD-319 limits from day one. Python PR 5 plans a large-stack thread and depth checks now.
Dart collector crash (SnapshotError, 3 causes) on a private repository
Fixed in #914 with facts and honest gaps. Frozen does not mean unmaintained. The corpus finds what fixtures miss.
Misleading diagnostics: 2 631 unresolved imports shown as parse_error
Fixed in #915 after 3 review rounds (one bad rebase undid #917, caught). Titles are shared constants now.
Published result schema changed in place (#915, first version)
Merged as command-result 12.0 (#915). 6.0 to 11.0 stay byte-identical; a test rebuilds 12.0 from them.
CI over budget: collectors area 4:47 to 17:37 min in one day, Full hit its 20-min limit
Owner: a target, not a gate. Limits become 40-min hang guards. #919 meets the budget; regular measured tuning.
14 needless repeats in one run: member inventory 10x, 89 % repeated ast.parse, facts 3x
D3 merged (#920): validations 3 to 1, ast.parse -82 %. D1 (#925): inventory 10 to 4, report 2 to 1. Rest: protocol 10.
Wrong number reported: host 82 of 92 s included a second collector run
Corrected: host 44 %. On the Python path the collector costs more, so PR 5 (Python in Rust) gains more.
Ratio flake 3.02: not a quadratic, but N runs and 2N runs not interleaved
Fixed in #917: runs interleaved, one child timed exactly, 300 s kill. Test files 438 to 391 s.
main red in Full for about 2 h: #915 was merged without a Full run
Fixed by #926 (it also found a real bug: language compared with is). New rule: a PR that changes an output gets one Full run.
1 Rust collector (scan.rs) and the store (capability set of a language)
2 Rust collector (module tree, symlinks, syn recursion)
4 check today (kind mapping), CLI and MCP (message); reason codes come with protocol 10
6, 8, 9, 10 engineering process: CI time, numbers, timing tests, merge rule
7 Python today: store (facts 3x, excerpts) and model/check (inventory 10x, report 2x)
What this means for the goal and the plan
The goal does not change: native collectors, a bounded host and a simple IR. The order does not change. Dates slip by about one fix round per collector PR.
Gate for every new collector: adversarial review (false PASS probes, deep and hostile inputs, symlinks) before merge. 5b-1 merges only when it is sound (5 review rounds).
New entry criterion: the CI budget (PR at most 10 min, Full at most 30 min). Order now: #919, #913 with Full, the 3a to 3c stack, 5b-1, then Python 0a and 0b.
Host time: D1 and D3 first, then P2 and P5. Then the honest benchmark 4.0.1 against main for Python, TypeScript and Rust (owner request).
Protocol 10 gets three concrete jobs from the audit: one collector process per command, layout from the raw model, and reason codes for gaps.
Process: reviews found 3 false PASS, 1 schema break, 1 pair loop and 1 crash case that the authors missed. Keep one independent review per PR.
M0: compiler oracle, profile by function, host against collector
TS calls: CBM typed 86.4 % recall without JSX, ArchKeel 14.8 %. React UI: collector 45 % of the time.
AD-314 is enforced. Protocol V9 carries the test scope. The pr-test list is outside the Full filter.
